01 / Signature

Recognisable at every scale.

The selected R, bowl and three-dot mark anchors the entire system. Preserve the supplied artwork; build the surrounding design around it.

The design idea

R identifies Roza. The bowl connects to food and preparation. The three dots suggest ingredients, experiments and shared discovery.

This is the proposed brand interpretation, not a claim about the original drawing process.

Position with purpose

Top-left on websites, posts and documents. Left chest on uniforms. At eye level on a dry entrance wall. Centred on a cup or video closing frame.

Protect the signature

Keep clear space of at least ¼ of the icon height. Use the full signature at 240 px digital width or 45 mm print width and above. Below this, use a separately prepared wordmark or icon master.

Starting production targets: proof at actual size. The small tagline is the first detail to lose readability.

Original proportions

Never stretch, tilt or redraw the wordmark.

Quiet background

Use a solid panel over busy photographs.

One master

Do not copy an AI-rendered wall logo into artwork.

Company line

Caroza Pvt Ltd on formal and closing applications.

02 / Logo family

A controlled set of variations.

One shape, four useful treatments. Colour changes the application, not the identity.

Primary / forest on ivory
Default for stationery, website headers and dry-wall signage.

Reverse / ivory on forest
Video endings, forest uniforms, outdoor ads and dark surfaces.

Single colour / charcoal
One-ink forms, stamps and economical printing.

Accent / forest + clay
Proposed campaign variant for large banners and editorial covers. Keep the primary version for formal documents.

These live colour variants use the supplied logo silhouette. A faithful vector master is still required for fabrication and precision multicolour separation.

Digital composition guide: 60% ivory / 25% forest / 10% sage / 5% accents. Interiors: let existing neutral finishes and oak dominate; use green in signage and selected details.

Text

Forest on ivory. Ivory on forest. Charcoal on sage. Use charcoal for small body text.

Materials

Matte painted signs, washable wall finishes, slate cabinets, oak details and forest textiles.

Type

Arial Bold for headlines and roles. Arial Regular for instructions. The logo remains custom artwork.

Bowl arcs and three dots form the supporting pattern. Use one large crop or a short stripe; keep it away from the logo’s clear space.

05 / Motion language

Move with intention.

The logo moves as one intact shape. Supporting dots and bowl arcs carry the playful motion.

CAROZA PVT LTD

Website scroll

During this section, translate the complete logo upward by 36 px and scale it from 0.88 to 1.00. Keep it readable throughout. Supporting shapes drift gently.

Video ident / 4 seconds

0–1.2 s: dots arrive in sequence.
0.6–1.6 s: full logo fades into place.
1.6–4 s: hold the complete signature and company line.

Motion boundaries

No spinning wordmark, letter distortion or constant bouncing. Avoid logo motion while viewers read a recipe or a result. Respect reduced-motion preferences.

Use this HTML as a motion specification and live preview. It is not an exported video file.

06 / People system

Five roles. One recognisable team.

Keep the supplied faces and role-specific wardrobe consistent across images, posts and video.

Chef

White coat + forest apron. Dark trousers and closed shoes. Hair restraint for preparation.

R&D specialist

White coat over dark clothing. Role badge and restrained hair for bench work.

Nutritionist

Sage shirt + charcoal trousers. Small forest chest mark.

Product & creative head

Forest polo + beige trousers. Ivory chest mark.

Marketing visual producer

Charcoal polo + dark trousers. Ivory chest mark; tied hair in the kitchen.

Chest embroidery: start with a 25–35 mm icon proof; apron: 70–90 mm icon proof. Avoid stitching the fine tagline at small size. Office outfits are not a substitute for task-appropriate protective clothing.

07 / Environmental identity

The room becomes a brand touchpoint.

Apply graphics to the existing space. These images show the visual direction; the supplied layouts control furniture and equipment placement.

Arrival & conversation

One primary wall signature. A sage glass arc and a short dotted stripe carry the pattern. Keep the original sofa, chair and circulation.

A place to focus

One nutritionist at the existing desk. Logo above desk, research sequence below. Keep four work positions and the floor clear.

Everyday hospitality

Existing fridge, cabinet, lever machine and dispenser. Apply small cup marks, restrained wall artwork and a fascia accent.

Ideas become decisions

Ivory logo on the clay panel. Forest notebooks and neutral sample jars. Branding stays behind the seated team.

Separate chef kitchen

Based on the separate kitchen drawing. Chef alone at the specified island. Forest fascia; wall mark on a dry upper surface. Keep worktops neutral.

Document the experiment

Application-room filming scene. Repeat the same uniforms and glass logo. Use small labels; avoid decorative clutter in real preparation areas.

AI photographic-style concepts, not actual premises or dimensionally verified construction views. Use the master logo for fabrication; do not trace generated signs.

12 / Quality control

Consistency is a daily practice.

Before publishing or producing any application, compare it with the master system.

Use

Original logo proportions.
Same staff faces and assigned uniforms.
Existing room furniture and clear circulation.
Natural food colours and believable work.
Short copy, legible contrast and calm margins.

Avoid

Recreated AI logos as production artwork.
Extra furniture to fill an image.
People standing through desks or crowding aisles.
Random colours, competing slogans or stretched marks.
Presenting generated concepts as actual staff photography.

Release checklist

Brand owner checks logo and message. Creative lead checks colour and layout. Facility lead checks spatial accuracy. Production supplier proofs actual size, material and legibility.

Digital colours are HEX references. Physical finishes require approved samples. Multicolour logo and environmental applications are design proposals. Keep the selected primary logo as the default.
